So each object is a connected component of non-background same color (4-connectivity), background mostcolor. Then for each object, applies corners: ulcorner, urcorner, llcorner, lrcorner of the object's bounding box? Actually corners of object patch (indices of object cells). Then shifts each by NEG_UNITY (-1,-1) for ul, UP_RIGHT (-1,1) for ur, DOWN_LEFT (1,-1) for ll, UNITY (1,1) for lr. Fills colors 1,2,3,4 at those shifted cells.

We need produce 3 input-output pairs. The student will see inputs and outputs. We can choose simple inputs. Need ensure verifier computes output. Need likely include multiple gray squares, perhaps different shapes/sizes? Rule: surround each square with four colored diagonal corners. The verifier uses corners of object, not necessarily squares. So any gray object (connected non-bg) gets four corner marks. If multiple objects, each object processed independently.

We need demonstrate enough for solver. We should include maybe one object, multiple objects, object not square? But task says sequence of gray squares. We can use squares. Need be careful about overlaps: if two squares close, their corner marks might overlap or conflict. The verifier processes all objects sequentially? Actually x1..x4 computed on all objects (apply over set). shift, fill each in order 1,2,3,4. Since apply over frozenset, order arbitrary but all same color mapping per corner type. So no conflict if same corner type overlaps? Overlap between different types could be overwritten by later fill (2 overwrites 1, etc). Better avoid overlaps to keep clean. We can make widely separated squares.

We need 3 demos. Use grids maybe 10x10. Need input grid integer colors 0-9. Background 0. Gray squares color 5. Non-background objects: if multiple squares same color 5, are they separate objects? objects with univalued True, diagonal False, without_bg True: it finds connected components of same value? Let's inspect objects function: for loc unvisited, val=grid[loc]. If val == bg (mostcolor) skip. obj={(val,loc)}; cands={loc}; while cands: for cand: v=grid[cand]; if (val==v) if univalued else (v != bg): add. So univalued=True: only same val as original. So each connected component of same color. Since all squares are 5 separated, separate objects. Good.

Need choose inputs that verifier can evaluate. Could use 10x10 with one square. But we want teach rule. Three examples should vary positions/sizes/number. But if we include multiple objects, output will show all. Let's craft.

But maybe there's subtlety: For a square, ulcorner is top-left cell of square, shift(-1,-1) gives cell diagonally up-left. urcorner top-right, shift(-1,+1) gives up-right. llcorner bottom-left shift(+1,-1) down-left. lr bottom-right shift(+1,+1) down-right.
